TASK: Implement the locked v2 run-record contract as a factory-layer module. Read factory/manager.py and departments/social/runtime/record.py first for the house style (logging module not print, stdlib only, no department names in factory code).

factory/runrecord.py must provide:
1. new_run_id() -> str — sortable unique id: UTC timestamp compact form + 8 hex chars of os.urandom, e.g. '20260802T194501Z-a3f9c2d1'. No external deps.
2. RunRecord validation: a build_record(**fields) -> dict function enforcing the contract: required keys {schema:'run-record/v2', rev:int, run_id, department, node, epoch, ts, attempt:int, round:int|None, release:{hash,source_ref}|None, trigger:{kind,id,dedupe_key}|None, engine:str|None, model:str|None, auth_class, usage:{input_tokens,output_tokens,cache_read,cache_creation}|None, cost:{lane,model_calls}|None, duration_ms:int|None, status, errors:list, artifacts:list, receipts:list, evaluator:dict|None, approval:dict|None, external_actions_taken:int}. Enforce enums: auth_class in {oauth_cli,service_oauth,local_model,blocked,None}; status in {ok,blocked,error,halted,killed,escalated,skipped}; trigger.kind in {time,event,goal,manual,escalation}. cost.lane in {flat_subscription,metered_forbidden}; building a record with lane='metered_forbidden' must still succeed but set a top-level violation flag field 'metered_violation': True (recording the violation is the point). Reject unknown top-level keys, reject non-int external_actions_taken. Raise ValueError with a message naming the bad field.
3. append_record(state_dir: Path, record: dict) -> Path — append one JSON line to <state_dir>/runs-v2.jsonl atomically and safely under concurrent writers: open with 'a', fcntl.flock exclusive around write+flush+fsync. Validate via build_record semantics before writing (validate_record(dict) helper). Never log or store prompt text/message bodies — the module has no field for them by design.

tests/test_runrecord.py — at least 8 tests including: id uniqueness+sortability across 100 ids; happy-path build+append+reload roundtrip; enum rejection for bad auth_class, bad status, bad trigger.kind (assert the error names the field); unknown-key rejection; metered_forbidden sets metered_violation flag; concurrent appends from 2 threads x 50 records produce exactly 100 valid JSON lines (no interleaving corruption); append creates parent dir if missing. Use tmp_path, no wall-clock flakiness (do not assert exact timestamps).

Verification a checker runs: pytest on your new test file must pass; you fail for touching any file outside the owned list or fewer than 8 new 'def test_' functions.
tasks.verified: a validated, enum-enforced, fcntl-locked runs-v2.jsonl writer exists at the factory layer with concurrency-proven tests

  factory/manager.py

THE TWO AUDITED DEFECTS (from a read-only audit with live evidence — fix both, change nothing else):

1. UNLOCKED WRITES. factory/manager.py writes STATE.json, runs.jsonl, and heartbeats.jsonl with plain open/os.replace and NO file lock, while other writers of these same files elsewhere in the codebase hold an fcntl lock (see departments/social/runtime/record.py::records_lock for the established pattern — read it, do not import it; factory code never imports department code). Production podcast runs.jsonl already shows two differently-shaped row types from the two differently-locked paths sharing one epoch counter. Under concurrent invocation the last os.replace silently wins and a cycle's findings are lost.
   FIX: create factory/lockutil.py with a records_lock(state_dir) context manager (fcntl.flock exclusive on <state_dir>/.records.lock, creating it if needed, always released), and make every manager write of STATE.json / runs.jsonl / heartbeats.jsonl happen under it. Keep writes atomic (temp file + os.replace for STATE.json; append+flush+fsync for the jsonl files). Preserve the module's model-free guarantee and its public function signatures.

2. ESCALATION REPLAY SPAM. Manager-originated escalations have no fingerprint dedup, so a persisting breach re-escalates every cycle. The proven pattern to copy lives in departments/podcast/runtime/escalate_outbox.py (durable-marker dedup) — read it as source material, do not import it or modify it.
   FIX: before recording an escalation, compute a stable fingerprint (department + finding code + subject), keep delivered fingerprints in <state_dir>/escalation_fingerprints.jsonl (append-only, written under the same lock), and skip re-escalating a fingerprint already present unless its 'resolved' marker row appears after it. Skipping must still be visible: the cycle's record notes 'escalation_suppressed_duplicate' with the fingerprint.

tests/test_manager_hardening.py — at least 7 tests: concurrent manager-style writes from 2 threads don't lose rows (write 50 each, count 100); STATE.json write is atomic under simulated crash (kill between temp write and replace leaves old state readable); lock file is created and released; same breach across 3 cycles escalates exactly once; a NEW distinct breach still escalates; suppressed duplicates appear in the cycle record; resolved-then-recurring breach escalates again. Use tmp_path fixtures and fixed timestamps; read existing tests in tests/ for the manager fixture style.

THE AUDITED DEFECT: departments/podcast/state/observations.jsonl grows unbounded (live: 11,166 lines, ~7 MB) and contains hundreds of exact-duplicate rows per (sensor, subject) pair from replayed sensor runs. Nothing rotates or compacts it. The reader (compare_charter.py — read it as source material, do not modify it) tolerates duplicates, so compaction must be safe and conservative.

BUILD: a standalone CLI tool rotate_observations.py (argparse; --state-dir required; --max-lines default 5000; --dry-run flag) that: (1) removes exact-duplicate rows — identical (sensor, subject, status, detail) where only ts differs — keeping the NEWEST of each duplicate group; (2) if still over --max-lines, archives the oldest overflow lines to observations-archive-<UTCdate>.jsonl in the same dir (append, never overwrite an existing archive); (3) rewrites observations.jsonl atomically (temp + fsync + os.replace); (4) prints a one-line JSON receipt to stdout: {kept, deduped, archived, dry_run}; (5) --dry-run changes nothing on disk but prints the same receipt shape; (6) malformed JSON lines are preserved verbatim at their position (never dropped silently) and counted in the receipt as 'malformed'. Use the logging module for diagnostics, never print except the receipt line. Exit 0 on success, 1 with a clear error message on unreadable input.

tests/test_rotate_observations.py — at least 6 tests: dedup keeps newest and removes exact copies; under-limit file with no dupes is untouched (byte-identical); overflow archives oldest lines and archive is append-only across two runs; --dry-run leaves file byte-identical while reporting counts; malformed lines survive and are counted; receipt JSON parses with all keys. Use tmp_path.

CONTEXT: Today no engine lane records model, tokens, or auth state. draft_post.py invokes engines from engines.example.yaml (claude_subscription uses '--output-format text') and captures only stdout text; qa_post.py likewise. The locked v2 contract needs per-call: resolved model name, usage token counts, duration, and auth_class — and on auth failure a 'blocked' outcome instead of a confusing error.

CHANGES:
1. engines.example.yaml — switch the claude_subscription command to '--output-format json' (keep --no-session-persistence and the other hardening flags). Add a per-engine optional 'auth_class' field (claude_subscription: oauth_cli, codex_oauth: oauth_cli) and an optional 'auth_probe' command field (documented comment; may be empty in the example).
2. draft_post.py — add a parse_engine_envelope(stdout: str, engine_cfg: dict) -> dict helper returning {model, usage:{input_tokens,output_tokens,cache_read,cache_creation}, duration_ms, raw_ok: bool}. It must: extract the FINAL complete JSON object from stdout (engines may print noise before it); tolerate missing fields by setting them to None (never invent numbers); on unparseable output return raw_ok False with the reason. Thread the parsed result into the existing draft receipt payload (N4-draft-r{N}.json gains 'model', 'usage', 'duration_ms', 'auth_class' alongside the existing bare 'engine' string) and into the run-record payload passed to record.write_record. When the engine config declares an auth_probe and it exits nonzero, do not call the model: write the receipt with status 'blocked', auth_class 'blocked', error code AUTH_EXPIRED, and return the blocked outcome to the caller.
3. qa_post.py — same envelope parsing and receipt enrichment for the QA call (N5-qa gains model/usage/auth_class).
Preserve all existing behavior, flags, shadow semantics, and the cross-model engine-choice logic. Never log prompt text or draft bodies in the new fields.

Mock subprocess — no real engine calls.
